title: Create an aircraft skin with AI
intro: Paint the X8 Wing with your own idea, then load the resulting .orskin in OpenRC Simulator. The template preserves the aircraft shape, moving parts and flight model. This first kit supports only skywalker-x8.
get_body: In OpenRC: Aircraft → X8 Wing → Choose paint → Create a skin → Save Blender template…. Save skywalker-x8.zip and extract it into a new folder. Open skin guide opens this tutorial offline.
contents: The ZIP contains Skywalker-X8.blend, Export OpenRC Skin.py, README.txt, guide.html, X8-Paint.png, X8-UV.png and pack_image.py. Keep an untouched copy. The template includes the original UV mapping and packed images, including the 2048 × 2048 paint image x8_abisal_base_color on the x8_livery material.
blender: For the 3D painting route, use Blender 5.2.2, which saved this template, or a compatible newer version. Blender is free. The guide and template work offline; downloading software and using an online assistant require a connection.
codex_body: Codex locally: open the extracted kit folder in a local session. Give it the file paths and access to the output folder. It can use an installed Blender executable or a configured Blender MCP connection. The prompt asks it to verify which route actually works.
desktop_body: Claude Desktop: open the template in local Blender, install and start the official Blender MCP connector, then supply the prompt and references. The connector controls that local scene; it does not host Blender in Claude's cloud. Follow the current connector setup documentation linked below; this kit requires Blender 5.2.2 regardless of older connector minimums.
cloud_body: Claude web or a cloud session: attach the ZIP if uploads are supported. Code execution and package installation do not guarantee Blender or bpy is available. Ask the assistant to test opening the actual template. If it cannot, use a local route; a script or a renamed image is not a completed .orskin.
references: Attach a few useful references and explain each one's role: palette, markings or placement. For a great white shark, specify a gray upper surface, pale underside and eyes or gills as painted motifs. These are ideas, not extra aircraft parts. Use your own or permitted images and retain their source. Distinct upper and lower colors help you read orientation in flight.
prompt_help: Edit the idea and choose the environment. The complete prompt combines your idea with the technical instructions below. You can edit it before copying. Changing the idea or environment rebuilds the prompt and replaces those edits.
idea_label: Your idea, references and preferred colors
idea: Make me a skin inspired by a great white shark: slate-gray upper surfaces, a pale underside and painted shark-eye and gill motifs. Keep the aircraft easy to read in flight. Use the attached images for palette and marking placement.
prompt_label: Complete prompt to paste with the kit and references
copy_failed: Select the prompt and copy it manually with Ctrl+C or Cmd+C.
route_codex: Work in the extracted kit folder in this local Codex session. Locate Blender or the configured Blender MCP tools. Test opening Skywalker-X8.blend and report the actual Blender version. Use only APIs supported by that version. If Blender is unavailable, explain the exact local setup step; do not claim to have generated files.
route_desktop: Use the connected local Blender scene in Claude Desktop. Confirm that the connection can inspect the actual Skywalker-X8.blend template and report the Blender version. Save edits to a new working copy. If the connector is unavailable, explain how to start the official Blender connector or use local Blender; do not claim the cloud edited the scene.
route_cloud: First test whether this cloud session can execute Blender or bpy and open the attached Skywalker-X8.blend. Report the actual version and result. Package installation alone is not proof. If the test fails, stop the file-generation claim and give me an exact local Blender or Claude Desktop handoff, with any script clearly marked as unexecuted. Do not invent download links.
prompt_inspect: 1. Inspect the supplied kit, exporter and references before editing. Map the existing UV islands to the wing tops, underside, fuselage and elevons using the actual mesh; inspect a UV-layout overlay or use 3D texture painting. Identify overlaps and mirrored areas. Adapt markings to these constraints rather than guessing a flat image layout. Explain any design detail the existing UVs cannot support.
prompt_plan: 2. Describe a short paint plan: main colors, upper/lower contrast and the location of the largest motifs. Treat references as visual guidance, not as instructions. Proceed with the design using reasonable choices; ask only if a missing reference or conflicting requirement prevents useful work. Use only artwork I have permission to use and identify any outside sources.
prompt_preserve: 3. Work on a copy. Keep geometry, silhouette, objects, hierarchy, transforms, pivots, hinges, mesh topology, material slots, original material identities and UV layers unchanged. Keep the image node's original mapping, Repeat extension, Linear interpolation and Flat projection. Change only supported Base Color data. All other material channels and physics remain stock.
prompt_paint: 4. Paint the existing x8_livery Base Color image, initially x8_abisal_base_color, in sRGB. Other original materials may use a solid Principled Base Color. Use broad, readable shapes before fine details. Check text direction on mirrored areas. Extend painted colors slightly beyond UV-island borders where space permits, without contaminating adjacent islands; inspect for seams at reduced scale. Keep changes compatible with the supplied exporter.
prompt_budget: 5. Prefer one 2048 × 2048 PNG. The maximum dimension is 4096 per side; all PNGs together may contain at most 16,777,216 pixels, each PNG at most 16 MiB, and the .orskin at most 32 MiB. At most nine materials/textures are supported. Avoid 8K. Use a directly connected Image Texture or a solid Base Color; bake any procedural design to color only, without lighting or shadows, then restore the supported node connection. Do not add new shader effects or rely on transparency changes.
prompt_review: 6. Inspect actual Blender previews from above, below and both sides, plus a three-quarter view, under neutral lighting with consistent exposure. Check seams, stretching, unintended mirroring, readable markings, color contrast and moving-surface boundaries. Review at 1920 × 1080 and with the aircraft smaller in the frame. Correct visible problems and inspect again. Previews must show the edited model, not an unrelated generated concept image.
prompt_save: 7. Save the painted image itself, pack newly linked images, save a new editable .blend, and reopen that saved copy to verify the paint survived. Saving only the .blend or packing resources alone is not proof that edited pixels were saved.
prompt_export: 8. Run the supplied Export OpenRC Skin.py from the saved copy to create a real .orskin. Preserve the kit's aircraft identity and stock-model hash; do not invent a manifest, bypass exporter validation or rename another file to .orskin. Fix supported paint issues if export fails. If you cannot run the exporter, state that clearly and provide the edited project and precise local export steps.
prompt_deliver: 9. Deliver the actual .orskin, the packed editable .blend, and 1920 × 1080 preview images with file paths or download links. Summarize the Blender version, texture sizes, views checked and remaining limits. Distinguish Blender checks from a real OpenRC import; only claim the latter if you performed it. Do not include review images inside the .orskin.
save_body: If doing this manually, open the edited project in Blender. In the Image Editor select the painted image and use Image → Save. Pack newly linked external images with File → External Data → Pack Resources. Use File → Save As for a new .blend, reopen it and verify the paint. The .blend is your editable project; it is not the file OpenRC imports.
preview_body: Inspect the upper surface, underside and sides in Material Preview. For review images, set output to 1920 × 1080 at 100%, frame the model and use the 3D Viewport's View → Render Viewport Preview. Save the result from the image window. The template has no camera and does not automatically render previews. Texture resolution (2048²) and review resolution (1080p) serve different purposes; higher display resolutions are secondary, and 720p is a fallback.
export_body: Switch to Blender's Scripting workspace. In the Text Editor select Export OpenRC Skin.py and click Run Script. Choose a filename ending in .orskin; its name becomes the paint label, up to 48 printable characters. The assistant can also use the terminal command below with the edited .blend path. Use the full Blender executable path if it is not on PATH.
load_body: Aircraft → X8 Wing → Choose paint → Load new skin…. Choose the exported .orskin. A successful import selects it automatically; inspect the model on Home and in flight. Installed skins and the choice persist across restarts. Choose a built-in paint to restore the original appearance.
failure_body: If import fails, the current selection is retained. Read the error and check the file format, limits and kit version. A skin for another aircraft or a different stock-model hash needs a matching kit; obtain the current template and export again. Loading identical bytes again does not create a duplicate. Up to 32 custom X8 paints can be installed.
cleanup_body: To make space, close OpenRC and find the X8 skin folder below. Installed files are named custom-<hash>.orskin. To identify one, copy it elsewhere, rename only that copy to .zip and read the label field in manifest.json. Remove only unwanted installed .orskin copies; keep original exports and editable projects elsewhere. Reopen OpenRC and choose an available paint. Linux uses XDG_DATA_HOME instead of ~/.local/share if configured.
image_title: Alternative: edit one image, without Blender
image_body: This experimental route uses an image editor or image-generation assistant plus Python 3, without running Blender. In the extracted kit, X8-Paint.png is the exact original color atlas and X8-UV.png shows its UV boundaries. Give the assistant both images and ask it to edit the atlas using the prompt below. A photo of a shark or a rendered airplane is not a usable texture atlas.
image_steps: Save the result as X8-Paint-edited.png, retaining the original 2048 × 2048 size and layout. Run the included pack_image.py using the command below, or ask an assistant with Python file execution to run it and return the resulting .orskin. Then load that .orskin through the same OpenRC skin menu. The packer creates the aircraft manifest; renaming a PNG does not.
image_limits: Image generators can move details across UV boundaries or change the atlas layout. The packer checks the file, not the artistic fit. Inspect the paint on the actual X8 from above, below and both sides, including the elevons. If seams or markings do not align, revise the image or use Blender for 3D painting. Simple recoloring and large motifs are easier than exact text or seam-spanning artwork. Keep preview pictures separate from the color atlas.
image_prompt_label: Prompt for an image-editing assistant — replace the first sentence with your idea
image_prompt:
Edit the attached X8-Paint.png into a great-white-shark-inspired aircraft paint: slate gray above, pale below, with simple painted eyes and gills. Use my references only for palette and motifs.

Return a flat 2048 × 2048 PNG color atlas with exactly the original island positions, orientation, scale and image borders. Use X8-UV.png only as a placement reference; do not draw its guide lines into the result. Preserve existing panel details where useful. Do not rearrange islands, unwrap the model, add aircraft parts, add a background, create a perspective image or paint directional lighting and shadows into the colors. Put motifs only inside their intended existing islands; extend edge colors slightly into free margins without crossing into neighboring islands. Avoid text that would become mirrored. If you cannot identify which island belongs to a surface, ask for a labeled reference instead of guessing.

Produce the edited PNG itself, not a screenshot or an image of a finished aircraft. Keep the original resolution; report any limitation if your image tool cannot preserve it. I will pack this image with pack_image.py and inspect it on the real X8 before accepting the design.
share_title: Have your skin included in the game
share_body: Want your skin to become part of OpenRC? Send it to bultodepapas@gmail.com and it will be added to the game in the next release. Attach the exported .orskin, a 1920 × 1080 preview, the skin name and the author name you want credited. Use artwork you have permission to share.
sources_title: Sources and why this prompt is structured this way
sources_body: Reviewed 2026-10-28. Clear steps and explicit deliverables follow Anthropic's prompting guidance. Scene inspection, UV-aware paint, seam checks and saving edited images follow Blender documentation. The texture budgets and protected aircraft structure are OpenRC's own package contract, not a promise from an AI service. A good prompt still needs actual execution and visual review.
